title: VPC edge telemetry footprint optimization notes
content:
Context and goal:
This doc is a working sketch for reducing the telemetry footprint (ingest, storage, egress) for private VPC/on‑prem deployments while keeping SLOs for latency and troubleshooting. Focused on small-to-medium customer sites (4–32 GPUs) where network costs and local storage are constrained.

High-level approach (priorities):
1) Reduce cardinality and high-churn metrics at the source (collector).
2) Use local short-term hot storage + tiered cold archive (S3-compatible or NFS) to limit long-term disk usage.
3) Selective sampling & adaptive scrape intervals per workload class.
4) Push more responsibility to the control plane for rollout decisions, but keep customers in control of data egress policies.

Quick architecture sketch:
- OTEL collectors as daemonset (k8s) or systemd services (baremetal).
- Fluent-bit (or vector) for logs, send to local log store (Loki or files) with shippers to object storage for retention > 7d.
- Prometheus using remote_write to a short-term TSDB (VictoriaMetrics single-node OR Thanos receive in larger sites).
- Grafana in read-only mode for customer dashboards, with alertmanager receiver local and optional federation to central ops for enterprise customers.

Collector configuration suggestions (OTEL):
- Metric accumulation: enable delta aggregation for counters and set histogram boundaries tuned to model token rates.
- Reduce high-cardinality labels: drop or hash user_id/session_id at the collector; keep service/model tags only.
- Enable resource detection but limit attributes (host, instance-type, model-name).
- Use batch span processor with max_export_batch_size tuned to < 200 to limit memory during bursts.
- Implement a lightweight processor to collapse repeated traces in short windows (heuristic dedupe for healthcheck noise).

Prometheus & scraping:
- Group scrape targets into 3 classes: control-plane (1s), serving runtime hot metrics (5s), infra/node metrics (15–30s).
- For internal model metrics (per-request latency distributions), consider exposing pre-aggregated percentiles instead of raw histograms.
- Leverage relabel_configs to drop labels that are not used in alerts/dashboards.
- Example relabel: drop label "request_id" and "user_email"; keep "model_name" and "route".

Remote write tiering plan:
- Local short-term retention: 7–14 days on fast disk (NVMe) for operational queries.
- Remote_write to cold store: compress and write every 30–60m to S3-compatible object storage; use Prometheus tools that create TSDB blocks (Prometheus remote_write adapters, vmagent).
- For small customers, recommend single-node VictoriaMetrics with data retention config instead of full Thanos.

Log shipping notes:
- Fluent-bit collects application stdout/stderr and structured JSON app logs. Route by log-level to different outputs.
- Critical alerts (error/warn with stack) -> route to immediate webhook + local alert index (small Elasticsearch or Loki index).
- Bulk debug logs -> buffered files, batched upload to object storage nightly.
- Avoid shipping raw token payloads; add scrubbing filter to remove PII and prompt/response bodies before leaving cluster (default on).

Grafana considerations:
- Ship a curated dashboard bundle: serving latency, request QPS, KV cache hit rate, GPU utilization, queue depth, and cost breakdown. Make these dashboards small (fewer panels) for edge sites.
- Disable user-created panels by default; provide safe templates only.
- Use snapshotting and export dashboards weekly for centralized observability team.

Terraform module notes (draft):
- Module: telemetry/collector
  - Inputs: collector_image, resource_limits, excluded_attributes, batch_config
  - Outputs: daemonset_name, service_account, configmap_hash
  - Implementation notes: allow toggling of "drop_high_cardinality_labels" and "sampling_rules" via variables.

- Module: telemetry/prometheus
  - Inputs: scrape_classes (map), remote_write_targets, local_retention_days, disk_class
  - Outputs: prometheus_statefulset, pvc_name, remote_write_config_hash
  - Important: provide boolean "use_victoriametrics" to switch implementation; be careful with PVC sizing defaults (don't pre-allocate >100Gi).

- Module: telemetry/logship
  - Inputs: backend_type (s3|loki|elasticsearch), retention_policy, scrub_rules
  - Outputs: fluentbit_configmap, secret_arn_placeholder

Upgrade plan checklist (from current 1.2.x collector to planned 2.0 telemetry):
- Pre-upgrade validation:
  - Snapshot current Grafana dashboards and Prometheus rule files.
  - Export promdata and verify remote_write target health.
  - Ensure backups of PVC volumes (velero or filesystem snapshots).
  - Validate disk usage < 70% in last 24h.

- Rolling upgrade steps (k8s):
  1) Drain a single node in canary AZ (if available), cordon so only collector pods move.
  2) Apply new collector config ConfigMap with feature flags disabled (e.g., advanced-sampling=false).
  3) Wait for new pods to be Ready and metric parity for core dashboards for 30m.
  4) Toggle advanced-sampling in small percentage of nodes (10%), observe ingestion rate and alert noise for 1h.
  5) If stable, roll out remaining nodes in waves.

- Fallback plan:
  - Have a job that can re-apply previous ConfigMap and restart collector pods within 5m.
  - Add temporary rule to drop remote_write traffic if ingestion spikes beyond expected (protects storage).

Operational runbook (short):
- High ingestion spike: check collector metrics for dropped spans, memory. If memory > 80% -> restart collector on node with backpressure enabled.
- Disk pressure: enable retention-pruner cronjob (delete > retention days) and offload older blocks to object storage.
- Missing dashboards: check grafana provisioning logs and configmap hash; reapply snapshot if necessary.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How aggressively can we sample model-internal metrics without affecting SLOs for debugging? Need per-customer experiments.
- Should we provide an "ultra-thin" packaging for tiny on-prem where only alerts are shipped and metrics are kept local for 48h?
- Cost model: estimate egress savings per 10k qps if we move from full metric export to 5x sampled export. (Finance + pricing input needed.)
- Add explicit compliance checklist for customers in regulated industries re: prompt redaction before any egress.

Immediate action items (next week):
- Marco: prototype collector relabel pipeline that hashes user identifiers and runs on sample cluster. (JIRA OBS-421)
- Evelyn: draft terraform inputs for telemetry/prometheus module switching to VictoriaMetrics fallback. (PR target: tf-modules branch)
- Samir: run cost-sensitivity analysis for remote_write frequency options and storage tiering.

Notes to self (minor):
- Keep playbooks brief: ops will copy/paste commands. Include kubectl/drain examples and velero snapshot commands.
- Avoid adding heavy default retention in terraform (let customer opt-in).

Useful commands (examples to include in final playbook):
- kubectl -n telemetry rollout restart daemonset/otel-collector
- kubectl -n observability port-forward svc/grafana 3000:80
- velero backup create promdata-2026-02-14 --include-namespaces observability
- vmctl snapshot export --retention-days 14 (victoriametrics helper)

References:
- internal: confluence/OBS/VPC+Telemetry+Blueprint (linked above)
- upstream: OTEL collector docs, VictoriaMetrics remote_write adapters, Fluent-bit filtering docs

This is intentionally a loose draft — want feedback on the sampling thresholds and the TF module inputs that should be optional vs required.
